task_brief: Mastery work on simple printmaking. Mastery: test a material or mark-making process through simple printmaking, then use observable evidence to explain or revise a learner-owned decision. Try the first small step yourself; a grown-up may read or demonstrate on separate material.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available for spoken reflection, explanation, or critique and scores the same. Use a written analysis, labelled plan, evidence table, notation, diagram, or private artifact check that preserves the stated target. No microphone, camera, recording, or public audience is required.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: You may use low-smell, low-dust materials, and you can sit or stand to work. Ask for chunkier handles or grips if that helps.
This work takes more than one sitting. Ask for a simple checklist with dates so you know what to do next. Keeping track is not part of your grade.
You can take a break, stretch, or come back to this later. That does not lower your score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, copyright, cultural context, and respectful representation.
No public performance, voice recording, photo, or camera use is ever required; provide a private, written, or no-audio alternative for every task.
Use only original student work, public-domain material, or properly licensed excerpts; never reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or protected works.
The final product must remain the student’s own authorship; adult or AI assistance may support planning and feedback but must not create the graded work.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting simple printmaking.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

remediation: Route 1: Reduce simple printmaking to three locatable events, areas, steps, or decisions. Label the intended effect beside each and underline the one tool pressure relationship that should carry it. Use a separate small study, four-event loop, thumbnail, evidence table, or paper plan. The adult may model the noticing process on different material but may not change the learner’s work. Check yourself: Point to or name the exact tool pressure evidence before deciding whether it serves the intent. New attempt: Put the support away and make a new arrangement, passage, response, or plan; record what the new evidence shows. Route 2: Return to the last understandable state. Hold every relationship steady except one chosen feature from tool pressure, direction, layering, joining, edge, surface, proportion, and safe control; predict what that single change should do. Test the feature on scrap paper, a silent count, a two-event rehearsal loop, movable shapes, or a short evidence sentence before changing the scored work. Check yourself: Name what stayed the same, what changed, and the first observable result—without using “better” as the evidence. New attempt: Create a different small case using the same one-variable method, then transfer the finding to the original task only if it serves the learner’s intent.
extension: Apply simple printmaking under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on simple printmaking rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.

age_policy.language: Short sections, one action at a time, and concrete noticing words.
age_policy.safety: Use familiar low-risk materials, stop or adjust any physical or sound action that causes discomfort, and require adult help for cutting, heat, fumes, or heavy equipment.
age_policy.privacy: Private work and self-critique carry full credit; no public display, identifiable media, account, or recording is required.

common_technique_errors.observable_mismatch: The stated intent for simple printmaking is present, but the record does not yet locate tool pressure, direction, layering, joining, edge, surface, proportion, and safe control that supports it.
common_technique_errors.not_an_error_when: The learner supports a different, ambiguous, subtle, or intentionally open effect with observable evidence.

common_technique_errors.observable_mismatch: Several relationships changed at once, so the learner cannot yet tell which choice caused the observed effect.
common_technique_errors.not_an_error_when: The task is an intentionally exploratory diagnostic and no causal claim is being scored.
